title: SLO-driven per-route dashboards and hot-path tracing for embed+rerank endpoints
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver SLO-aligned observability for embeddings + rerank endpoints focused on per-route visibility, hot-path tracing for tail latency, and cost-per-request breakdowns. This ticket scopes the implementation plan, dashboard templates, trace sampling policy, alert rules, and rollout steps for production traffic. Motivation: customers require fine-grained visibility into why rerank requests spike cost or latency on specific routes and which model/config permutations (quantization, batch size, model_variant) drive regressions. Current state: global metrics exist (overall embedding qps, average latency) but we lack per-route token-level cost attribution, rerank score distributions over time, and consistent trace spans that capture embed->search->rerank critical path across services.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route Grafana dashboard template deployed (route tag) showing: P50/P95/P99 latency, token counts, per-token cost, QPS, batch size distribution, model_variant split, rerank score histogram, and tail latency contribution from each span

Distributed traces capture embed call, vector-search, and rerank scoring spans with consistent tags (route, request_id, customer_id, model_variant, batch_size) and root span latency >= 99th percentile sutability
Cost-per-request calculation available in metrics (USD/token and USD/request) with breakdown by model_variant and quantization profile

Alerting rules defined and implemented: route-level latency burn rate (P99 > SLO for 15m), cost spike (3x baseline for 5m), and rerank-quality regression alert (rank-correlation drop detected via eval proxy), each with runbook links
Sampling policy implemented: 1% uniform sampling + adaptive 100% sampling for requests breaching latency threshold or error rate; traces retained for 30d in prod for flagged routes
Runbook and on-call playbook added to Confluence with triage steps, dashboard links, and rollback guidance
Instrumentation landed behind feature flag; smoke-tested on staging; gradual rollout to 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic with metrics validated at each stage
updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff meeting with PM (Riley Chen), Design (Maya Singh), and infra SMEs. Agreed SLO targets: P95 latency 120ms for small-embed routes, P95 250ms for large-embed rerank routes.
2025-02-25: Prototype dashboard widgets created in Grafana; initial metric names proposed: rerank.latency_ms, embed.token_count, rerank.score_dist, cost.usd_per_request.

2025-02-28: Tracing spec drafted — span names: span.embed.request, span.vector.search, span.rerank.score; required tags documented. PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/2124 (instrumentation scaffolding).

2025-03-03: Telemetry review completed with Observability team. We will add route and model_variant tags to all embed/rerank metrics and normalize attribute keys. Decided to use adaptive sampling to avoid trace explosion.
2025-03-06: Feature flag gate added (ff: embedding_rerank_obsv_v1). Staging rollout planned for 2025-03-07. Assigned verification to QA (Hannah Lopez).
implementation_notes: Metric tagging: use 'route' label derived from API route and 'model_variant' from model metadata. Emit token_count at embed request end. Emit cost_estimate token_cost * token_count as prometheus metric (cost_micro_usd to avoid floats). Tracing: propagate request_id and customer_id through RPC. Use OpenTelemetry library used across the platform. Dashboard panels should support route filter and customer_id drilldown. Use precomputed histograms for score distributions. Avoid high-cardinality tags in long-term metrics; customer_id should be on traces and logs only, not on Prometheus aggregated metric series.
tradeoffs:
- High-fidelity per-customer metrics would be useful but would create cardinality explosion in Prometheus; we restrict customer-level data to traces/logs and enabled 'customer' delta counters for top-20 customers only.
- Full 100% trace sampling would be ideal for debug but is too costly; adaptive sampling balances cost vs visibility.
- Enriching every span with model weights/quantization profile increases span size; we limit to 'model_variant' and 'quant_profile' tags only.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge instrumentation behind feature flag (staging), 2) Validate dashboards in staging with synthetic load, 3) Enable on 10% of production traffic for 48h and validate metrics and alert noise, 4) Expand to 50% for 24h, 5) Full rollout and schedule a follow-up incident review after 7 days.
test_plan: - Unit tests for metric emission and tag normalization, - End-to-end test generating synthetic requests through embed+rerank and validating trace spans and dashboard panels, - Load test to ensure metrics ingestion scales at expected QPS, - Canary verification checklist for each rollout phase.
